observation: The whole set in the opening position, inspected in all three supplied views. FRONT: the board reads as one flat slab of even thickness with the pieces standing on it; the row seen edge-on climbs in size with no piece sunk below or floating above the field, and the two star flames rise from the middle of the row without touching a neighbouring piece. TOP: sixteen worlds sit one to a cell in the two home ranks, each disc centred in its own cell with clear air to the next; twelve cocoa belt tiles fill the two middle blocks of the field; the Sol star and its two flames occupy the lower den group and the Anti-Sol star the upper one, each with its three corona wells around it. Nothing overlaps a cell boundary, nothing is doubled and no cell is empty that should be filled. ISO: the same arrangement in relief -- discs proud of the field, belt tiles flush, corona wells recessed, stars standing proud -- with the two storage trays beside the board. URANUS, the pair this revision changes: both pieces are visible as cyan balls carrying a white hoop and NOTHING ELSE. In the top view, where their poles are nearest the lens, each globe is one uniform cyan disc with no pale patch, cap or panel anywhere on it, which is the negative requirement this round has to see. The two hoops lean opposite ways, one per army. SATURN beside them still reads as a different kind of ringed piece -- a flat brim wider than its ball against a hoop standing over its ball -- now that both rings are the same white. PROPORTION: the size ladder is legible in the front and iso views, Mercury smallest and Jupiter largest, and every piece stands on the same diameter disc, which is correct. TWO KNOWN RENDERER ARTEFACTS, not part defects and not new to this revision: the Anti-Sol star's black core renders as a void because the renderer shades flat with no shadow and no ground plane, and for the same reason the two trays appear to float beside the board rather than resting with it.
